decisive_items: Cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay: positive
vitreous cell and haze obscuring retinal vascular details, blurred disc margins, and superonasal peripheral retinal whitening
response.rationale: CSF TPHA and RPR confirm syphilis; bilateral ocular inflammation with vitritis, disc edema, and retinitis localizes the infection to the eye, making ocular syphilis the best specific diagnosis.

rejected.why: Retinal findings are better explained by confirmed syphilis; no herpetic or other viral cause was identified.
Captures retinitis but omits the prominent anterior uveitis, vitritis, and disc involvement.
Confirms the systemic infection but is too broad; ocular syphilis is the indicated diagnosis.
HIV retinopathy does not account for positive syphilis serologies, CSF TPHA, and spirochetes on skin biopsy.
Runner-up; uveitis is supported but the full retinal and optic disc findings are better covered by ocular syphilis.
Severe immunosuppression is a predisposing factor, not the specific cause of the ocular syndrome.
